parts.text: Royal Mail: your parcel is on hold
because of an unpaid shipping fee of £1.45.
parts.why: Small surprise fees are a classic hook.

parts.text: Pay within 12 hours
parts.why: A tight deadline is pressure to stop you thinking.

parts.text: or it will be returned to the sender.
royalmail-redelivery-uk.com
parts.why: Not an official Royal Mail address.

investigations.explanation: Check deliveries on the official website or app, never through a link in a text.

parts.text: Dear Customer,
parts.why: A generic greeting instead of your name.

parts.text: after our annual calculation you are owed a tax refund of £468.20.
Claim within 24 hours
parts.why: Urgency again.

parts.text: at hmrc-gov-refunds.net
parts.why: Official HMRC sites end in gov.uk.

parts.text: and enter your card details to receive it.
parts.why: Refunds never need your card details.

parts.text: Kind regards, HM Revenue & Customs.

investigations.explanation: HMRC doesn't send refund links. Forward scam emails to phishing@hmrc.gov.uk and texts to 7726.

parts.text: Hello, this is the fraud team at your bank.
We've spotted suspicious payments on your account.
To keep your money safe, move it to a new safe account now,
parts.why: Banks never ask you to move money to a safe account.

parts.text: don't tell anyone, not even staff in your branch,
parts.why: Asking for secrecy is a huge red flag.

parts.text: and read me the code we've just sent to your phone.
parts.why: One-time codes are for you only.

investigations.explanation: Hang up and call 159 or the number on your card, ideally from a different phone.

parts.text: I turned £250 into £8,000 in three weeks!
parts.why: Huge fast returns are the hook.

parts.text: Guaranteed profits, zero risk.
parts.why: No real investment is guaranteed.

parts.text: My account manager trades for you,
just send your deposit in crypto.
parts.why: Crypto payments are almost impossible to recover.

parts.text: Only 5 places left this week!
parts.why: Fake scarcity to rush you.

parts.text: Link in bio.

investigations.explanation: Check firms on the FCA Register and Warning List before investing.

parts.text: Work from home as a Payments Assistant.
Earn £500 a week, no experience needed.
parts.why: High pay for no experience is a warning sign.

parts.text: Receive payments into your own bank account and send them on to our partners,
parts.why: This is money muling, and it's illegal.

parts.text: keeping 10% for yourself.
parts.why: A cut for moving money is how mule recruiters tempt people.

parts.text: Flexible hours.

investigations.explanation: Never let anyone move money through your account.

parts.text: Brand new games console, still sealed.
£120 (normally £450).
parts.why: A price far below normal is the bait.

parts.text: Bank transfer only, no PayPal.
parts.why: Refusing protected payments removes your buyer protection.

parts.text: I'm working abroad, so a courier will deliver it.
parts.why: A seller you can't meet, plus a courier story.

parts.text: Happy to send more photos.

investigations.explanation: Use protected payments and see items in person when you can.

parts.text: MEGA CLEARANCE: 90% off all designer trainers!
parts.why: Unrealistic discounts on brands.

parts.text: Free UK delivery on orders over £50.
Pay by bank transfer for an extra 10% off.
parts.why: Pushing bank transfer means no card protection.

parts.text: Questions? Email shopdeals2026@gmail.com
parts.why: A real retailer uses its own email domain.

parts.text: Returns accepted within 14 days.

investigations.explanation: Check reviews and company details, and pay by card.

parts.text: Hi Mum, I dropped my phone in the bath.
This is my new number.
parts.why: A new number stops you checking with the real person.

parts.text: Can you pay a bill for me today? It's urgent.
parts.why: An urgent money request is the whole point.

parts.text: I can't talk on the phone right now,
parts.why: Avoiding a call stops you hearing it isn't them.

parts.text: love you x

investigations.explanation: Call them on their old number before sending anything.

parts.text: Ofgem: Energy Bill Rebate 2026.
You are entitled to a rebate of £315.
parts.why: Ofgem regulates energy. It doesn't email people rebates.

parts.text: To receive it, confirm your bank details
parts.why: Asking for bank details to “pay” you is a giveaway.

parts.text: before midnight tonight
parts.why: Artificial deadline.

parts.text: via ofgem-rebates-uk.com.
parts.why: Not an official gov.uk or ofgem.gov.uk address.

investigations.explanation: Any genuine energy support comes via your supplier or gov.uk, not a random email.

parts.text: Hi! I'm Sophie from a recruitment agency.
parts.why: Unsolicited job offers on WhatsApp are a common scam opener.

parts.text: We pay £100–£300 a day for liking videos online.
parts.why: Unrealistic pay for trivial tasks.

parts.text: You'll get small payments at first to build trust.
To unlock higher-paying tasks, just top up your account with a deposit.
parts.why: Paying to earn is the core of “task scams”.

parts.text: Reply YES to start.

investigations.explanation: Real employers never ask you to pay to work.

parts.text: Hi, I'd like to buy your sofa. I'll pay full price.
I've sent the money, check your email for the PayPal confirmation.
parts.why: Fake payment emails are used to rush you. Check the PayPal app itself.

parts.text: I accidentally sent £200 too much, please refund the extra by bank transfer.
parts.why: Overpayment refund requests are a classic trick.

parts.text: My courier will collect,
but you need to pay their £50 insurance fee first.
parts.why: Sellers never need to pay a buyer's courier.

investigations.explanation: Only trust payments you can see in your own account or app.

parts.text: ALERT: A new payee “J SMITH” was added to your account.
If this wasn't you,
call us urgently on 0800 046 1234.
parts.why: Never call a number given in an unexpected message. Use the one on your card.

parts.text: Your account will be frozen in 1 hour otherwise.
parts.why: Threats and deadlines are pressure tactics.

parts.text: Do not use your banking app as it may be compromised.
parts.why: Steering you away from your real app is a giveaway.

investigations.explanation: Check your banking app or call 159.

parts.text: PARKING CHARGE NOTICE.
You have parked in a restricted zone.
Pay £60 within 24 hours to avoid a £150 penalty.
parts.why: Extreme urgency is a pressure tactic.

parts.text: Scan the QR code to pay now.
parts.why: QR codes on unexpected notices can lead to fake payment sites.

parts.text: Payments accepted by bank transfer only.
parts.why: Legit operators offer proper payment options.

investigations.explanation: Check the operator independently and pay only through official channels.

parts.text: Your TV Licence Direct Debit has failed.
Your licence will be cancelled today
parts.why: Urgent cancellation threats are typical.

parts.text: unless you update your payment details
at tvlicensing-renewals.co.uk.
parts.why: Check the address carefully. Lookalike domains are common.

parts.text: Dear Valued Customer,
parts.why: Generic greeting.

investigations.explanation: Go to the official site by typing the address yourself.

parts.text: Lovely 2-bed flat in Zone 2, only £700 a month!
parts.why: Rent far below market rate.

parts.text: I'm the landlord but I'm working abroad,
parts.why: An owner who can't show you the property.

parts.text: so I can't show you around.
Send the deposit and first month's rent
parts.why: Paying before viewing is how renters lose money.

parts.text: and I'll post you the keys.

investigations.explanation: Never pay before viewing, and use a protected deposit scheme.

parts.text: Good morning, I'm calling about an exclusive opportunity.
parts.why: Unexpected calls about investments are a major red flag. Pension cold calling is illegal.

parts.text: Our clients earn 12% a year, guaranteed.
parts.why: Guaranteed returns don't exist.

parts.text: We're not on the FCA Register yet because we're so new,
parts.why: Unauthorised firms leave you without protection.

parts.text: but you need to decide today.
parts.why: Pressure to decide now.

parts.text: I'll send you a brochure.

investigations.explanation: Hang up, then check the firm on the FCA Register and Warning List.

parts.text: DVLA: we were unable to process your latest vehicle tax payment.
You are owed a refund of £58.10.
parts.why: Surprise refunds are a classic hook.

parts.text: Claim within 24 hours
parts.why: A tight deadline.

parts.text: at dvla-refund-uk.com
parts.why: Official DVLA sites are on gov.uk.

parts.text: using your card details.
parts.why: Refunds never need your card details.

investigations.explanation: Vehicle tax services are only on gov.uk. Forward suspicious texts to 7726.

parts.text: Dear Resident,
parts.why: A generic greeting.

parts.text: following a band review you are due a council tax rebate of £297.
To receive payment, log in to your online banking
parts.why: Nobody needs your banking login to pay you.

parts.text: through the secure link below
parts.why: Links in unexpected emails can lead to fake sites.

parts.text: before Friday.
parts.why: Pressure to act fast.

investigations.explanation: Contact your council using the details on its official website.

parts.text: Your membership is on hold.
We couldn't verify your payment details,
so your account will be closed in 24 hours.
parts.why: Threats of closure create panic.

parts.text: Update your card here: stream-billing-help.net
parts.why: Not the service's real domain.

parts.text: Thanks, The Support Team

investigations.explanation: Open the app or type the official address yourself to check your account.

investigations.source: Phone call from “your bank's security team”

parts.text: We think your card has been cloned.
To protect you, please install the SecureHelp app
parts.why: Remote-access apps let scammers control your phone.

parts.text: so we can check your phone
and keep this call confidential
parts.why: Secrecy is a red flag.

parts.text: while we move your money to safety.
parts.why: Banks never move your money to “safety” for you.

investigations.explanation: Hang up and call 159 or the number on your card.

parts.text: VIP signals group: we tell you exactly which coin to buy before it pumps!
parts.why: “Pump” groups profit by dumping on members.

parts.text: Last week members made 400%.
parts.why: Huge past returns are bait.

parts.text: Join for £99 a month.
Buy as soon as we post the coin, no questions!
parts.why: Pressure to act without thinking.

parts.text: Not financial advice.

investigations.explanation: Pump-and-dump schemes leave late buyers with the losses.

parts.text: BREAKING: Famous TV presenter reveals the trading app that made her millions.
parts.why: Fake celebrity endorsement.

parts.text: Banks are furious and want this taken down!
parts.why: Drama to stop you thinking.

parts.text: Start with just £250.
Our account manager will call you within the hour.
parts.why: High-pressure follow-up calls are part of the scam.

parts.text: Spaces limited.
parts.why: Fake scarcity.

investigations.explanation: Celebrities' images are routinely used in fake investment ads. Report them to the platform.

parts.text: Hi, I'm calling about a free pension review.
parts.why: Pension cold calling is illegal in the UK.

parts.text: We can unlock your pension early, even though you're only 45.
parts.why: Early release usually means huge tax charges or theft.

parts.text: Our overseas investment pays 9% guaranteed.
parts.why: Guaranteed high returns don't exist.

parts.text: You just need to sign the transfer today.
parts.why: Pressure to sign now.

parts.text: Can I take your pension details?

investigations.explanation: Hang up. Check any firm on the FCA Register and talk to MoneyHelper, which is free.

parts.text: Congratulations! Your loan of £5,000 is pre-approved,
parts.why: Approval before you've even applied is a warning sign.

parts.text: even with bad credit.
To release the funds, pay a £75 insurance fee
parts.why: Upfront fees to release a loan are a classic scam.

parts.text: by bank transfer
parts.why: Unprotected payment.

parts.text: today.

investigations.explanation: Genuine lenders don't ask for fees before paying out a loan. Check firms on the FCA Register.

parts.text: New government scheme: write off up to 80% of your debt!
parts.why: There's no magic government write-off. Real debt solutions have rules and consequences.

parts.text: Limited places available.
parts.why: Fake scarcity.

parts.text: Reply YES and we'll call you.
Small admin fee applies.
parts.why: Free debt advice exists, so paying a fee is a red flag.

parts.text: Text STOP to opt out.

investigations.explanation: Get free debt advice from StepChange, Citizens Advice or MoneyHelper.

parts.text: This tiny plug-in gadget cuts your electricity bill by 90%!
parts.why: Impossible claims.

parts.text: Energy companies HATE it.
parts.why: Drama to stop you thinking.

parts.text: Only £39.99, today only.
parts.why: Fake deadline.

parts.text: Thousands of 5-star reviews.
Free delivery.

investigations.explanation: No plug-in gadget slashes bills like this. Most are useless or unsafe.

parts.text: Beautiful puppies ready now, £400.
parts.why: A price far below normal for the breed.

parts.text: I'm working away so I can't show you in person,
parts.why: You can never meet the seller or see the animal.

parts.text: but send a £150 deposit by bank transfer
parts.why: Unprotected payment before seeing anything.

parts.text: and the courier will deliver.
parts.why: Fake courier fees often follow.

parts.text: Lots of photos available.

investigations.explanation: Always see a pet with its mother in person before paying anything.

parts.text: Stunning seaside villa, half the usual price for August!
parts.why: Too cheap for peak season.

parts.text: Book direct with me to avoid fees.
parts.why: Taking you off the booking platform removes its protection.

parts.text: Pay the full amount by bank transfer
parts.why: Unprotected payment.

parts.text: to my personal account.
parts.why: Not a business account.

parts.text: Free airport pickup.

investigations.explanation: Book through reputable platforms and pay by card.

parts.text: 2 tickets for the sold-out arena show,
face value, can't go anymore.
PayPal Friends & Family only, no Goods & Services.
parts.why: Friends & Family removes buyer protection.

parts.text: Need it gone tonight, others are interested.
parts.why: Pressure.

parts.text: Account created last week.
parts.why: New accounts are a common sign of ticket fraud.

investigations.explanation: Buy resale tickets through official resale platforms.

parts.text: Earn £400 a week from home as a Parcel Inspector!
Receive parcels at your address,
parts.why: Using your address to receive goods bought with stolen cards.

parts.text: repackage them and post them abroad
parts.why: “Reshipping” jobs are a money-laundering scam.

parts.text: using the prepaid labels we email you.
Paid monthly, no interview needed.
parts.why: No interview for a paid job is a warning sign.

investigations.explanation: Reshipping jobs can involve you in crime. Real employers interview you.

parts.text: Hi! I saw your CV online and you're perfect for our £45k remote role.
parts.why: Unsolicited offers that are too good.

parts.text: The interview will be by text chat only.
parts.why: Scammers avoid voice or video.

parts.text: Please send your passport photo and bank details
parts.why: ID and bank details before any offer is identity fraud bait.

parts.text: so we can set up your payroll today.
We'll send you equipment money by cheque.
parts.why: Fake-cheque overpayment scams often follow.

investigations.explanation: Never send ID or bank details before a verified job offer.

parts.text: Hi, quick update from your supplier:
our bank details have changed.
parts.why: Changed bank details are the core of invoice fraud.

parts.text: Please pay this month's invoice to the new account below.
Don't call, we're having phone issues.
parts.why: Stopping you from checking is a giveaway.

parts.text: Kind regards, Accounts.

investigations.explanation: Always confirm new bank details by calling a number you already have.

parts.text: 🎉 We're giving away 100 free phones to celebrate our anniversary!
parts.why: Fake giveaways copy real brands.

parts.text: Just like, share
and pay £1.99 postage
parts.why: Small fees harvest card details, often for hidden subscriptions.

parts.text: via the link in our bio.
parts.why: An unknown link.

parts.text: Winners announced today!
parts.why: Urgency.

investigations.explanation: Check the official account (verified, old, lots of real followers) before entering anything.

parts.text: Welcome to the Wealth Circle! I'm your mentor, Professor James.
parts.why: Fake “mentors” are a hallmark of investment group scams.

parts.text: Members made 30% this month following my picks.
parts.why: Unrealistic returns.

parts.text: Download our special trading app
parts.why: Fake apps show fake profits.

parts.text: and deposit at least £500 to unlock VIP signals.
Withdrawals open after 90 days.
parts.why: Delayed withdrawals hide the fact your money's gone.

investigations.explanation: Unregulated “clubs” and apps are a top route for investment fraud.

parts.text: I've loved getting to know you these past weeks.
I'm serving overseas and can't video call for security reasons.
parts.why: Always a reason not to video call.

parts.text: I need £800 for my leave papers so I can finally meet you.
parts.why: A money request from someone you've never met.

parts.text: Please send it by gift cards.
parts.why: Untraceable payment.

parts.text: Don't tell your family, they wouldn't understand.
parts.why: Isolating you from others.

investigations.explanation: Never send money to someone you've only met online.

parts.text: WARNING! Your computer is infected with 5 viruses!
parts.why: Scary pop-ups are fake alerts.

parts.text: Do not close this window
parts.why: Pressure to stay.

parts.text: or your files will be deleted.
Call Microsoft Support on 0800 123 4567 now.
parts.why: Real tech firms don't put phone numbers in pop-ups.

parts.text: Error code: 0x80070005

investigations.explanation: Close the browser. Never call numbers from pop-ups or allow remote access.

parts.text: New device added to your account: iPhone 15, Manchester.
If this wasn't you, reply NO
parts.why: Replying lets them call you back pretending to be the bank.

parts.text: and our fraud team will call you shortly.
parts.why: Scammers phone right after these texts.

parts.text: Do not log into your app until we call.
parts.why: Steering you away from your real app.

investigations.explanation: Check your banking app yourself, or call 159.

parts.text: This is HMRC. You owe £1,240 in unpaid tax.
A warrant will be issued for your arrest today
parts.why: Threats of arrest are a scare tactic.

parts.text: unless you pay right now
parts.why: Pressure.

parts.text: using supermarket gift cards.
parts.why: No tax authority accepts gift cards.

parts.text: Stay on the line.
parts.why: Keeping you from checking.

investigations.explanation: HMRC won't threaten arrest or ask for gift cards. Hang up and report it.

parts.text: Congratulations! You've been selected to win a brand new laptop!
parts.why: You can't win a draw you never entered.

parts.text: Just complete a short survey
and pay £2.95 delivery
parts.why: Small fees can start hidden subscriptions.

parts.text: within 10 minutes
parts.why: An artificial timer.

parts.text: to claim your prize.

investigations.explanation: Real prizes don't require fees.

parts.text: You have been selected for a £650 student support grant.
parts.why: Unexpected grants are bait.

parts.text: Verify your identity
by entering your bank login
parts.why: Nobody legitimate needs your bank login.

parts.text: at student-grants-gov.co
parts.why: Not a gov.uk address.

parts.text: by midnight.
parts.why: Urgency.

investigations.explanation: Student finance only uses official gov.uk services.

parts.text: Hi, we're offering you a free upgrade to the latest phone.
To confirm, I'll text you a code,
please read it back to me.
parts.why: That code can hand over your account or approve a SIM swap.

parts.text: We just need your online account password too.
parts.why: Never share passwords.

parts.text: This offer ends today.
parts.why: Pressure.

investigations.explanation: Call your network on its official number to check any offer.

parts.text: Hi, I'll buy your bike for the full price.
I've paid through the marketplace's courier service.
To receive the money, click this link and enter your card details:
parts.why: Sellers never enter card details to receive money.

parts.text: marketplace-safe-pay.com
parts.why: A fake payment page.

parts.text: Hurry, the payment expires in 30 minutes.
parts.why: Pressure.

investigations.explanation: Only accept payment inside the platform's own app.

parts.text: Hey, sorry to bother you!
I accidentally sent you a 6-digit code,
parts.why: That code is for taking over YOUR account.

parts.text: can you forward it back to me?
parts.why: Their account has probably been hacked.

parts.text: It's urgent, I'm locked out.
parts.why: Urgency.

parts.text: Thanks x

investigations.explanation: Never share verification codes, even with friends. Turn on two-step verification.

parts.text: URGENT: families left homeless by the floods need your help NOW.
parts.why: Urgent emotional pressure.

parts.text: Every £10 feeds a family for a week.
Please donate by bank transfer
to our coordinator's personal account.
parts.why: Real charities don't use personal accounts.

parts.text: We're too new to be registered yet.
parts.why: Check that charities are registered.

investigations.explanation: Check a charity on the Charity Commission register and donate through its official website.

parts.text: I'll buy your car, but I'm abroad.
parts.why: A buyer who can't see the car.

parts.text: I'll pay via my vehicle escrow service, it's safer for both of us.
parts.why: Fake escrow sites are a common trick.

parts.text: Just give my shipping agent the car and keys
parts.why: Handing over the car before the money is in your account.

parts.text: once you get the escrow email.
parts.why: Fake emails can look official.

parts.text: I've bought cars this way many times.

investigations.explanation: Only hand over a car once the money has cleared in your own bank account.

parts.text: Try our premium meal planner FREE for 3 days!
Just enter your card details to start.
After your trial, £49.99 per month
parts.why: An expensive subscription buried in the terms.

parts.text: billed automatically,
parts.why: Auto-renewal you might miss.

parts.text: cancel by calling our office during business hours only.
parts.why: Hard-to-cancel terms are a trap.

investigations.explanation: Note the end date and how to cancel before you start any free trial.

parts.text: Prestige Capital Partners: authorised by the FCA.
For enquiries, call our dedicated line on 07700 900123
parts.why: Clone firms list real firm numbers but their own contact details.

parts.text: or email prestigecap@outlook.com.
parts.why: A real firm uses its own email domain.

parts.text: Bonds paying 10% fixed, capital guaranteed.
parts.why: High guaranteed returns are a scam signal.

investigations.explanation: Check the FCA Register and contact the firm only on the details listed there.

parts.text: You've earned £3.20!
Upgrade to Gold Member for £20
parts.why: Real survey sites are free.

parts.text: to unlock surveys paying £50 each.
parts.why: Unrealistic pay.

parts.text: Withdrawals only for Gold Members.
parts.why: Locking your earnings behind payment.

parts.text: 98% of members upgrade!

investigations.explanation: Never pay to unlock earnings.

parts.text: Your balance: £186.40!
To withdraw, first top up £50
parts.why: Paying to withdraw your own money is a classic trap.

parts.text: to verify your account.
Complete 3 more tasks after topping up
parts.why: The goalposts keep moving.

parts.text: and your VIP level unlocks bigger rewards.
parts.why: “Levels” keep you depositing.

investigations.explanation: If you have to pay to get your earnings, there are no earnings.

parts.text: Earn 15% cashback everywhere!
parts.why: Far above normal cashback rates.

parts.text: Link your bank account
by entering your online banking username and password
parts.why: Never give anyone your banking login.

parts.text: in our app.
Bonus £20 if you sign up in the next hour.
parts.why: Pressure.

investigations.explanation: Genuine apps use your bank's own secure Open Banking screen, never your password.
